title: "Choropleth maps in R with canvasXpress"

author: "Isaac Neuhaus"

A choropleth map shades each region by a value — emissions, population, votes, incidence. The
trick is always the same: join a table of values to a set of map shapes by a common key, then
pick a color scale. In this post we build one in R with [canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org):
you pass a named vector of values and a topoJSON of boundaries, and the join and coloring happen
inside the render, so the result is interactive and fully reproducible from a single spec.

## One value per region

A choropleth needs exactly one measurement per shape. In canvasXpress the **columns** are the
regions (they match the map by name) and the **row** is the variable you color by — here CO₂
emissions per country for 2018. We'll load a prepared table; swap it for your own (any
`country → value` table works).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

y <- read.table(
  "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-dat.txt",
  header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "", row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

dim(y)              # 1 row (CO2) x N countries
y[, 1:4]
```

The single row is the variable (`CO2`); each column name is a country that must match a shape in
the map. An optional **sample annotation** table (rows = countries) rides along for richer
tooltips and legends — here the continent and ISO code.

```{r}
x <- read.table(
  "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/r/cX-CO2-smp.txt",
  header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "", row.names = 1,
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
head(x)
```

## The map

`graphType = "Map"` with a `topoJSON` of world boundaries draws the shapes; `colorBy = "CO2"`
shades each country by its value. The countries join to the map by name — no manual merge, no
projection math.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data     = y,
  smpAnnot = x,
  graphType = "Map",
  colorBy   = "CO2",
  topoJSON  = "https://www.canvasxpress.org/data/maps/WORLD.json",
  mapId     = "countries",
  legendPosition = "left",
  theme = "solarized",
  title = "CO2 Emissions per Country (2018)",
  width  = 700,
  height = 500
)
```

Each country is shaded by its emissions, the legend maps color to value, and hovering a country
shows its name, continent and number. The whole figure is one portable spec — the data, the
boundaries and the color rule travel together.

## Beyond the world map

Point `topoJSON` at a different boundary file to map US states, a single country's provinces, or
a custom region — the join key is just the shape name. Switch `colorBy` to a categorical column
(e.g. an election winner) for a qualitative map, add `decorations` to drop labeled markers on
cities, or set `mapProjection` for an Albers or Mercator view.
